description: Chlorine is a chemical element with symbol Cl and atomic number 17, and is the second-lightest of the halogens. It is a yellow-green gas at room temperature that is extremely reactive and a strong oxidising agent, with the highest electron affinity and third-highest electronegativity among the elements. All chlorine in the Earth's crust exists in the form of ionic chloride compounds, and it is the second-most abundant halogen and 20th most abundant element in Earth's crust.
uses: Elemental chlorine is commercially produced from brine by electrolysis in the chloralkali process and is used in the manufacture of a wide range of consumer products, including polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and many intermediates for plastics. It is used as a common disinfectant in swimming pools and drinking water, and has served functions in topical antisepsis and public sanitation. The high oxidising potential of elemental chlorine led to the development of commercial bleaches, disinfectants, and chemical reagents for many industrial processes.
characteristics: Chlorine is a yellow-green gas at room temperature that melts at −101.0 °C and boils at −34.0 °C, with a melting and boiling point intermediate between fluorine and bromine. It has an electron configuration of [Ne]3s23p5 and is one electron short of a full octet, making it a strong oxidising agent with properties intermediate between fluorine and bromine. The colour fades at low temperatures, so solid chlorine at −195 °C is almost colourless.
